quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When used on roadways, bicycles are considered:

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles on the road. Bicyclists and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you while driving at night, you should:

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch your lights to high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights blind you, look at the right edge of the road instead of ahead. This keeps your car on the road until you pass the other vehicle.

questions.question: If you want to pass a pedestrian walking on the roadway and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, you should:

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
Keep driving at a steady speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk your horn to get the pedestrian to move over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. If you need to pass a pedestrian but an oncoming vehicle is coming, slow down and let that vehicle pass first. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: The amount of alcohol in the blood is called:

options.text: Implied consent (IC).
Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).

questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. A higher BAC means more impairment.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on the highway, you should:

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Park with all four wheels off the road, if possible.
Stop where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park with all four wheels off the road, if possible.
questions.explanation: If your car breaks down, move it completely off the road if you can.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Do not enter.
Roundabout ahead.
No U-turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that U-turns are not allowed here.

questions.question: When may drivers stop in travel lanes?

options.text: When they're lost.
When they are dropping off a passenger.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never stop in travel lanes for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.question: Collisions are more likely to happen when:

options.text: All vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.
One lane of traffic is traveling faster than the other lanes.
One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Collisions happen more often when one driver travels faster or slower than other vehicles. Driving too fast or too slow increases your risk of a crash.

questions.question: When it is very foggy, you should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Turn your lights to high beams.
Turn your lights to low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your lights to low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off moisture and create glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: You are in a minor collision at an intersection with no injuries and little damage. You should:

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if possible.
Not move your vehicle for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if possible.
questions.explanation: After a minor collision with no injuries, move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.

questions.question: Why is it more dangerous to drive at night than during the day?

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
The road is always more slippery at night.
Your reaction time is slower at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead because of low light and glare from oncoming headlights. Always use your headlights and drive carefully in the dark.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through the zone quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
Keep your normal speed through the zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down and be prepared to stop. Follow posted speed limits and watch for workers and changing conditions.

questions.question: Your vehicle's wheels run off the edge of the pavement. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the front wheels slightly left to get back on the road.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently brake.
Brake hard and turn the front wheels sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently brake.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, hold the steering wheel steady, let off the gas, and brake gently. Slow down, check for traffic, then safely return to the road. Do not jerk the wheel sharply, as this can cause you to lose control or enter other traffic lanes.

questions.question: As you drive faster, it is important to:

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look far ahead of your vehicle.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances. When driving fast, look far ahead so you have time to safely react to dangers.

questions.question: One solid yellow line and one broken yellow line mark the center of the road. If the broken yellow line is next to your lane, it means:

options.text: You cannot pass other vehicles.
You can pass other vehicles on the left if no traffic is coming.
You can only turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles on the left if no traffic is coming.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to your lane means you can pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: Head restraints should be:

options.text: Adjusted to touch the back of your head.
Removed from the seats if possible.
In any position, as they have no real effect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adjusted to touch the back of your head.
questions.explanation: Head restraints prevent whiplash injuries when hit from behind. Adjust them to touch the back of your head.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash.
Higher speeds mean you need more distance between you and other cars.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the risk of death in crashes. At speeds over 80 mph, survival is unlikely. Higher speeds also mean you need more distance to stop, so increase your following distance as you speed up.

questions.question: This sign warns that the road ahead:

options.text: Turns sharply right, then left.
Curves right, then left.
Curves right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a reverse curve. The road curves right first, then curves left.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light means:

options.text: The same thing as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
The same thing as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop completely. Check that the way is clear, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go. This is the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?

options.text: When the driver you passed signals you to return.
After you signal for three seconds.
When you see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your lane, make sure you are not too close to the vehicle you passed. When you see both of its headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough space to safely return to your lane.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Look through the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Rely only on your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: When backing up, place your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly through the rear window. Mirrors do not show what is directly behind your vehicle. Always back up slowly.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: When pavement is wet, reduce your speed.
The road ahead winds in a series of turns or curves.
Traffic increases ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pavement is wet, reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the road will be slippery when wet. You should slow down.

questions.question: When must drivers use their headlights?

options.text: One half hour after sunset until one half hour before sunrise
During the day in clear weather
When they are tired

questions.correctAnswerText: One half hour after sunset until one half hour before sunrise
questions.explanation: Use your headlights from one half hour after sunset until one half hour before sunrise. Also use them at any other time when you cannot see 200 feet ahead.

questions.question: You hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked vehicle or other property, you must leave a note with your name, phone number, and address on the vehicle or property you hit.

questions.question: At an intersection with stop signs on all corners, yield to any driver:

options.text: On your left.
Who arrived before you.
Across from your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Who arrived before you.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles go through in the order they arrived. If multiple vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
